items.actClause: AN ACT to direct the metropolitan transportation authority and the New York city transit authority to study aboveground transit infrastructure
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5754

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to direct the metropolitan transportation
authority and the New York city transit authority to study aboveground
transit infrastructure

 PURPOSE :

Directs the metropolitan transportation authority and New York City
transit authority to study and report on the aboveground transit
infrastructure of the metropolitan transit authority

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of this bill directs the metropolitan transit authority and
the New York city transit authority, in consultation with the
department of environmental conservation and the department of health,
to conduct a study relative to the amount of lead paint abatement at
aboveground stations; the degree to which the authority is in
compliance with the federal Clean Air Act; to establish
recommendations to further lead paint abatement; and, to determine the
fiscal impact of recommendations.

Section 2 directs the metropolitan transit authority and the New York
City transit authority to publish a report of their findings to the
governor, temporary president of the senate, speaker of the assembly,
and the mayor of the City of New York.

Section 3 sets forth an immediate effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

In 2017, the Metropolitan Transit Authority's 7 Line celebrated its
100th anniversary. While countless New Yorkers and visitors to New
York City have benefitted from use of the Authority's subways in the
past century, so too have stations shown their signs of wear and tear.

Recent media reports have indicated that among these signs of aging,
sizeable paint chips have started to chip away from aboveground
stations on the 7 Line, often falling onto the sidewalks and streets
below. As much of the paint utilized at these aboveground stations is
in many cases as old as the stations, falling paint chips reportedly
include lead.

It is now well known that exposure to lead can result in extensive
damage to a person's brain and central nervous system, causing a coma,
convulsions, and even death. Particularly vulnerable to the negative
effects of lead exposure are young children, and it is unacceptable
for aboveground stations to persist as a potential source of lead on
streets located below.

This legislation is necessary to for the Authority to determine the
extent of lead abatement that has occurred at all of its aboveground
stations, tracks and trestles under its control to date, as well as
for the Authority to eliminate any dangers from lead paint that may
still exist.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

None. New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Nominal.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 58 Chapter 492
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 5754-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to direct the metropolitan transportation authority and the
        New York city transit authority to study  above  ground  transit
        infrastructure"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill would direct the Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA)
and  New  York  City  Transit Authority (NYCT), in consultation with the
Department of Health and the Department of  Environmental  Conservation,
to  study any lead abatement that has occurred at above-ground stations,
trestles, and tracks, and to make recommendations regarding the need for
further remedial efforts.
 
  For decades, however, the MTA has  funded  efforts  to  safely  remove
degraded paint from its elevated tracks, trestles, and stations, includ-
ing  those  located on subway lines and commuter railroads. The MTA then
repaints those structures in a manner that protects  from  any  possible
lead  exposure and ensures they can withstand a variety of environmental
factors. The MTA's work is subject to rigorous procedures for containing
and collecting degraded paint before repainting.
 
  Rather than conduct a new study, the Executive has secured  an  agree-
ment  with  the  Legislature to pass legislation in the upcoming session
that will require the NYCT to provide an annual report  identifying  all
current  or  planned  capital projects involving the removal of existing
lead-based paint from above-ground tracks, trestles, and  stations.  For
each  project, NYCT will describe the work to be performed and the meas-
ures that will be taken to protect the public's health and safety.    On
this basis, I am signing this bill.

  This bill is approved.                      (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                                ______
